stories.title: The roster goes deeper: nine new watches land
stories.summary: Baltic brings a titanium diver, a 1940s-style three-hander, and real stone dials; William Wood adds bronze and the Fire Exit day-date; Vero lands a Portland-built manual-wind and its U.S. Forest Service field watch.
stories.body:
This drop is all depth — nine new watches across four roster brands, every one in current production.

Baltic contributes three: the Aquascaphe Titanium, a 300m Grade 5 titanium diver on the Miyota 9039; the HMS 003, a 36.5mm three-hander with a stepped five-piece case and sector dial straight out of the 1940s; and the Prismic Stone, a 9.2mm-thin hand-wound cocktail watch whose dial is a genuine slab of cut mineral — pietersite, pink albite, dumortierite, or bloodstone — so no two are alike.

William Wood adds its Bronze Collection diver, whose crown inset is brass melted down from a century-old British firefighter's helmet, and the Fire Exit Watch — a Sellita SW220 day-date under a green glass dial styled on a fire-exit sign, with a day wheel that has the running exit-sign man doing something different every day of the week.

And from Portland: Vero's Meridian Manual Wind, a California-dial hand-winder assembled and regulated in-house around a Sellita SW-210, plus the Forest Service Edition — a Cerakote field watch developed with the U.S. Forest Service, its colorways keyed to wildland-fire roles, with a portion of sales supporting conservation work.

All nine are in the deck now. Swipe on.

stories.title: Trafford breaks its own rules: the Core line is always in stock
stories.summary: The Daytripper Core and Touring GMT Core go live July 22 — one colorway each, no limited seasonal drop, first shipments in September.
stories.body:
Trafford has built its reputation on limited seasonal drops — miss the window, miss the watch. The new Core line breaks that rule on purpose.

From July 22 you can order a Daytripper Core in Blue ($799) or a Touring GMT Core in White ($899) any day of the year. Both carry the same Miyota 9075 true-GMT caliber as their limited siblings — the hour hand jumps independently for painless time-zone changes — in a 39mm 316L steel case with sapphire front and rear, rated to 100m. First shipments land in September.

One colorway per model, always available: the Core line is Trafford's answer to everyone who found the brand five minutes after a drop sold out.

stories.title: Furlan Marri, Hora Pictor, Vero & Clemence complete the roster
stories.summary: Four more independents land on WatchSwipe — GPHG-recognized neo-vintage from Geneva, Portland-built tool watches, and two of Britain’s most talked-about young brands.
stories.body:
The WatchSwipe roster is complete: ten independent brands, every one hand-picked.

Furlan Marri (Geneva, 2021) needs little introduction — seven months after launching on Kickstarter, its neo-vintage Havana chronograph won the GPHG Horological Revelation prize, and the Havana Salmon became an instant collector favorite. The mechanical Flyback and hand-wound Disco Volante now sit above it in the range.

Hora Pictor (Hong Kong, 2024) brings true metier d'art to the deck: every dial is hand-fired Grand Feu or cloisonne enamel over silver leaf, one at a time, by founding enamel artist Eriks.

Vero (Portland, 2015) assembles, services, and warranties every watch out of its Oregon shop, and its collaborations keep the catalog unmistakably American — 10% of every Smokey Bear watch funds wildfire prevention with the U.S. Forest Service.

Clemence (Edinburgh, 2021) is the climate-positive pick: founder Tom Clemence plants a native Scottish tree for every watch sold, and the Photic MKII diver has drawn praise from Fratello and Worn & Wound.

Every model and colorway is live in the deck now. Happy swiping.

stories.title: Five independents join the deck
stories.summary: Studio Underd0g, Baltic, Trafford, William Wood, and Brew arrive on WatchSwipe — twenty watches spanning watermelon chronographs to firefighter heritage.
stories.body:
WatchSwipe's catalog just grew by five of the most-loved independent brands in modern watchmaking, each with its four most popular models.

Studio Underd0g (London, 2020) built a cult following in record time with pun-named dégradé dials — the Watermel0n chronograph is already an icon — every piece hand-assembled in Britain by a single technician.

Baltic (Paris, 2016) is the vintage-inspired standard-bearer of French microbrands: the Aquascaphe diver, the micro-rotor MR01 dress watch, the rugged little Hermétique, and the panda-dial Scalegraph, all assembled in Besançon.

Trafford (Austin, 2020) tells American stories in color — Hill Country wildflower dials on the Crossroads S, guitar-legend colorways on the Touring GMT, and a Kickstarter-born racing chronograph honoring WWII spy-drivers.

William Wood (Newcastle, 2017) honors the founder's firefighter grandfather: upcycled fire-hose straps, crowns cast from melted fire-helmet brass, and a range that runs from the Valiant diver to the Triumph chronograph.

Brew (New York, 2015) designs watches around the espresso ritual — chronograph scales sized to a 25–35 second pull, cushion cases inspired by vintage espresso machines. Coffee culture, on the wrist.

Every model and colorway is live in the deck now — swipe through and find your favorites.

stories.title: Astor + Banks brings Chicago watchmaking to WatchSwipe
stories.summary: The veteran-founded independent joins the deck — officer's watches, a dual-crown tool diver, and a field watch, all assembled in Chicago.
stories.body:
Astor + Banks has been assembling watches in Chicago since 2012, when Army veteran Andrew Perez named the brand after the Gold Coast street corner where he lived. The catalog that lands on WatchSwipe today shows how far an American independent can push at these prices.

The Fortitude line is the heart of it: officer's-style everyday watches at 38.5mm, with the Lite offering a slim no-date take at $650 and the Pro adding HV1200-hardened steel and 20,000A/m anti-magnetic protection. Both run Miyota automatics adjusted in-house.

At the tool end sits the Sea Ranger M2 — a dual-crown design whose internal 12-hour ring gives you a second time zone, rated to 1000ft and powered by a Swiss LJP G100 with a 68-hour reserve. The Terra Scout rounds out the range: a sandblasted field watch under box sapphire, with a full-lume dial option that glows edge to edge.

Swipe through all four models now, including every production colorway.

watches.description: The civilian take on Astor + Banks' officer's-style Fortitude: slimmer case, clean no-date dial, and a Miyota 9039 automatic adjusted in-house. Applied markers and hands glow with BGW9 Super-LumiNova, and the tapered 20mm bracelet hides polished chamfers on the underside of the links. Anti-magnetic to the ISO 764 standard and water resistant to 660ft — an everyday watch that punches far above $650.

The flagship officer's watch, updated: steel hardened to HV1200 for scratch resistance, anti-magnetic to 20,000A/m — over four times the ISO requirement — and a Miyota 9015 automatic adjusted in-house. Heat-blued hands on select dials, BGW9 lume throughout, and the same perfectly tapered bracelet as the Lite. Formal to casual, 38.5mm, any day of the week.

watches.caseMaterial: Brushed 316L steel, HV1200 coating, soft-iron anti-magnetic plates
watches.description: A dual-crown, go-anywhere tool watch two years in the making. The top crown drives an internal 12-hour rotating ring — a second time zone without a GMT movement — while the Swiss LJP G100 automatic runs a 68-hour reserve, adjusted in-house to ±8 seconds a day. Rated to 1000ft with hardened HV1200 steel and a soft-iron anti-magnetic cage. Bracelet versions include a color-matched FKM rubber strap ($1,149 on strap only).

A modern interpretation of the classic military field watch: tough, legible, reliable. The 3-layer matte dial sits under box sapphire, the sandblasted 38.5mm case wears 46mm lug-to-lug, and the Swiss LJP G100 automatic is adjusted in-house to ±8 seconds a day with a 68-hour reserve. Ships with both canvas and FKM rubber straps and a Horween leather watch wallet. Desert Sand limited edition $1,195; the full-lume dial option glows edge to edge.

The 01Series is Studio Underd0g's third-generation flagship chronograph and the watch that put the brand on the map: a 38.5mm x 12.9mm 316L steel case driving a hand-wound Chinese Seagull ST-1901B bicompax movement (21,600vph, 50-hour power reserve with the chronograph stopped). Its lead dial, Watermel0n, uses a two-tone red-over-green dégradé finish that has been the brand's signature design since its 2020 launch. The case carries a sapphire crystal, 5 ATM (50m) water resistance, and a quick-release leather strap fitted by The Strap Tailor.

The 02Series is Studio Underd0g's homage to WWII-era "Dirty Dozen" military field watches, built around a 37.5mm x 11.5mm 316L steel case and a hand-wound Swiss Sellita SW200-2 M movement with a 63-hour power reserve and hacking seconds. Its lead colorway, Nightshade, pairs a sunburst deep-purple dial with aged orange numerals and a distressed leather strap to mimic decades of wear. The multi-layer dial uses a 1mm tinted sapphire top-disc over a sunray brass base with X1 Super-LumiNova lume, and the case is rated to 10 ATM (100m).

The 03Series is Studio Underd0g's premium monopusher chronograph, cased at 38.5mm x 13.6mm in 316L steel and powered by a hand-wound Sellita SW510 M (Spécial/Élaboré grade, ±5 s/d accuracy, 63-hour reserve) operated by a single cam-actuated pusher instead of the usual two. Its lead colorway, Salm0n, sets a salmon-pink tachymeter rim against a radial-brushed grey dégradé dial. At £1,750 it is the brand's highest-priced core-range model, rated to 5 ATM (50m) water resistance with a sapphire crystal.

The Cocktail Collection is a run of limited-edition collaborations between Studio Underd0g and historic British watchmaker Fears, sharing a 38mm x 12mm cushion-cased 316L steel case (10 ATM/100m) and a hand-wound Sellita SW200-2 M movement. Each release is named after a cocktail and sold in small batches at watch fairs: the lead colorway, Gimlet, was limited to 200 pieces at British Watchmakers' Day 2025 and reportedly caused a stampede on release, followed by the 300-piece Manhattan at WindUp Watch Fair NYC and The Mimosa. All three carry FEARS-branded dials with a sapphire crystal and typically sell out within their launch window.

Aquascaphe Classic is Baltic's signature dive watch and, per the brand's own "Most popular" homepage ranking, its best-selling model. The 39mm stainless steel case runs a Miyota 9039 automatic movement with a 42-hour power reserve, backed by 200m of water resistance and a double-dome sapphire crystal. Its sandwich dial construction — a Baltic hallmark — creates deep, three-dimensional markers at 3, 6 and 9 filled with Super-LumiNova C1, finished off with a 120-click unidirectional bezel and a screwed crown.

MR01 is Baltic's micro-rotor dress watch, the #2 model in the brand's own "Most popular" homepage ranking. It is built around the Hangzhou CAL5000a automatic micro-rotor caliber — a thin, self-winding movement usually reserved for far pricier dress watches — inside a 36mm stainless steel case topped with a high-domed hesalite crystal for a vintage look. The 42-hour power reserve movement is rated to just 30m water resistance, reflecting its dress-watch brief, and ships on an Italian calf leather strap. The line also includes a guilloché-dial "Roulette" variant alongside the plainer railroad-track "Classic" dial shown here.

Hermétique is Baltic's field/adventure watch, appearing more times than any other line in the brand's own "Most popular" homepage ranking. The compact 37mm stainless steel case runs a Miyota 9039 automatic movement with a 42-hour power reserve, under a double-dome sapphire crystal, with an integrated crown keeping the profile clean. It carries an unusually rugged 150m water resistance rating for a field watch. The same case and movement are sold in two dial-color families — the muted, canvas-inspired "Tourer" palette and the brighter, beach-toned "Summer" colorways.

Scalegraph Classic (still widely known by its earlier name, Tricompax) is Baltic's flagship three-register "panda dial" chronograph, the modern descendant of the twin-register Bicompax that helped launch the brand's 2017 debut. Its "Panda" colorway is the only chronograph to make Baltic's own "Most popular" homepage ranking. The 39.5mm stainless steel case is powered by a hand-wound Sellita SW510-M movement with a 63-hour power reserve, under a double-dome sapphire crystal and an aluminum tachymeter bezel, rated to 50m water resistance.

The Crossroads S is the newest generation of Trafford's flagship Crossroads line: a square case marketed as 'wears like 40mm' but actually 35mm x 36mm and just 9mm thick, with a 46mm lug-to-lug. It is powered by a hand-wound Sellita SW-210 built in La Chaux-de-Fonds and assembled in Porrentruy, the first Trafford watch to carry a Swiss Made designation, regulated to +/-5 seconds/day with a 42-hour power reserve. The 316L stainless steel case has a scratch-resistant hardening coating and a double-domed sapphire crystal with interior anti-reflective coating, rated to 10 ATM (100m). It ships on a color-matched leather strap, with an optional H-link steel bracelet available as an add-on.

watches.crystal: Domed sapphire, interior AR coating, front and rear
watches.description: The Touring GMT runs on the Miyota 9075 'True GMT' automatic movement, regulated in-house to +/-10 seconds/day at 28,800 vph with a 42-hour power reserve. The 39mm 316L stainless steel case is 46mm lug-to-lug and 12mm thick, with a screw-down crown and screw-down case back rated to 10 ATM (100m), and sapphire crystal with interior anti-reflective coating front and rear. Season Two's four colorways are named for guitars/guitarists (Clapton's Slowhand, Hendrix's Izabella, McCartney's Lefty, Cobain's Daphne) and each ships on a matching leather strap with contrast stitching.

watches.crystal: Sapphire, interior AR coating, front and rear
watches.description: The Daytripper is powered by a Miyota 9075 automatic movement reworked to spotlight its quick-set hour hand, letting wearers jump the local hour forward or back without disturbing the running minutes or seconds, at 28,800 vph with a 42-hour power reserve. The 39mm 316L stainless steel case (12mm thick, 46mm lug-to-lug) has a scratch-resistant hardening coating and sapphire crystal front and rear, rated to 10 ATM (100m). Season Two adds a fully lumed BGW9 Super-LumiNova chapter ring and four gradient dials, each named for a different time of day, on a color-matched leather strap.

The S.O.E. Roadster was Trafford's debut model (originally Kickstarter-funded), inspired by three 1930s Grand Prix drivers -- Robert Benoist, Jean-Pierre Wimille, and William Grover-Williams -- who were recruited into Britain's WWII-era Special Operations Executive, with each colorway named for one of them and finished in his signature racing color. It runs on a Seiko VK64 meca-quartz chronograph movement with a sweeping central chronograph hand and a 24-hour subdial, visually inspired by the Bugatti Type 35 race car. The 43mm case (41mm excluding the bezel) is 48mm lug-to-lug and about 12.8mm thick, with hands and markers lumed in BGW9 Super-LumiNova, rated to 100m water resistance, and ships with both a leather strap and a matching nylon strap.

The Valiant is William Wood's flagship automatic diving watch, built around a 41mm 316L stainless steel case, a Seiko NH35 automatic movement with a 41-hour power reserve, and a double-domed sapphire crystal tinted blue in tribute to founder Jonny Garrett's grandfather's 'Blue Watch' shift pattern at the Newcastle & Gateshead Fire Brigade. Its crown is cast from brass melted down from a genuine 100-year-old British firefighter's helmet, and every colorway ships on a quick-release strap made from upcycled fire hose or a stainless bracelet. The dial's chequered seconds track is lifted from the livery on the side of a British fire engine, and the case is rated to 100m water resistance.

watches.crystal: Sapphire, low-flush curve, anti-reflective coating, blue-tinted
watches.description: The Chivalrous is William Wood's dress-watch line, pairing a 41mm stainless (or rose-gold-plated) case with a Swiss-Made Ronda 762 quartz movement and a sunburst dial set with a Roman numeral at 12. Its signature detail is a commemorative coin let into the caseback, cast from brass melted down from an original 1920s British firefighter's helmet and sealed under its own sapphire window. Finished with a low-flush, anti-reflective sapphire crystal and offered on fire-hose, leather, or steel-bracelet straps, it carries a 50m water resistance rating.

watches.caseMaterial: 316L stainless steel (gold-plated on the Vintage Edition)
watches.crystal: Sapphire, low-flush curve, anti-reflective coating, blue-tinted
watches.description: The Triumph is William Wood's chronograph collection, cased at 41mm in 316L stainless steel (gold-plated on the Vintage Edition) around a Swiss-Made Sellita SW510 chronograph movement with a 48-hour power reserve and brass chronograph pushers. Twin sub-dials at 3 and 9 o'clock are styled after fire-hose pressure-pump gauges, and the seconds track reproduces the chequered pattern from the side of a British fire engine. Rated to 100m water resistance under a double anti-reflective sapphire crystal, it ships on fire-hose, fire-gear, or steel-bracelet straps depending on colorway.

watches.caseMaterial: Stainless steel with black PVD coating
watches.crystal: Sapphire, anti-reflective coating, blue-tinted, exhibition caseback window
watches.description: The Fearless is William Wood's smallest and stealthiest model, a 39mm stainless steel case finished in matte black PVD around a Seiko NH35 automatic movement with a 41-hour power reserve. Its exhibition sapphire caseback is engraved with a modern British firefighter's helmet motif, and the crown is cast from brass melted down from a genuine 100-year-old firefighter's helmet, carrying the same material story used on the Valiant. Charcoal-effect dials with rose-gold, lume-filled indices sit under an anti-reflective, blue-tinted sapphire crystal, and the case is rated to 100m water resistance.

The Metric is Brew Watch Co.'s flagship chronograph, built around a cushion-shaped case that recalls 1970s motorsport chronographs, blending brushed and polished stainless steel 316L for contrast. It runs a Hybrid VK68 meca-quartz chronograph movement behind a sapphire crystal, in a 36mm-wide by 41.5mm lug-to-lug case rated to 5ATM (50m). It anchors Brew's lineup and is offered in the widest range of colorways of any Brew model, from mirror steel and PVD black to gold-toned and patterned dials.

Metric Lite is Brew's most compact watch, reworking the Metric's tonneau case into a clean three-hand, 30mm-wide (34mm lug-to-lug) piece with no chronograph complication. It swaps the flagship's meca-quartz module for an automatic 6T27 movement, keeping the same sapphire crystal, stainless steel 316L case, and 5ATM (50m) water resistance. Colorways lean toward quieter, vintage-inspired dials: brushed steel, PVD gold, and gemstone finishes such as tiger's eye, mother-of-pearl, and Tahitian pearl.

Super Metric shares the standard Metric's 36mm by 41.5mm cushion case, Hybrid VK68 meca-quartz chronograph movement, sapphire crystal, and 5ATM (50m) water resistance, but pushes the dial design further with bold color-blocked chapter rings, dual-finish subdials, and an anodized-aluminum chronograph pusher for a spot of accent color. It reads as the more graphic, motorsport-flavored sibling to the standard Metric dials. Electric Blue, Burnt Orange, Royal Blue, and Lumina Yellow give the line a higher-contrast identity within the Metric family.

The Retrograph is Brew's most literal expression of its coffee-culture identity: Brew built its 38mm by 41.5mm meca-quartz chronograph specifically as a utilitarian, retro timing device whose 60-minute totalizer tracks a 25-35 second espresso shot, alongside other timed durations. The lead Espresso colorway pairs a rosegold PVD-plated stainless steel case with a chocolate-espresso sunburst dial and brown leather strap; sapphire crystal and 5ATM (50m) water resistance carry across the line.

Totem Cipher pairs a cloisonné enamel dial with Ancient Greek numerals inspired by the Rosetta Stone, its abstract totem shapes outlined in fine silver wire, hand-filled with enamel, and fired at high temperature. It runs a Swiss Sellita SW200 Elaboré automatic movement (28,800 vph, 41-hour power reserve) in the brand's standard 38mm 316L steel case with sapphire crystal front and back and 50m water resistance. At $4,092 it is Hora Pictor's most expensive model and headlines the "Totem" section of the brand's Watches page. It is offered in a single dial colorway.

Volcano Grey layers grey enamel over hand-applied silver leaf, inspired by submarine volcanic eruptions where molten rock meets the ocean floor; the same silver-leaf enamel styling (site-marketed as "Smoked Ocean") is shared across its Twilight Violet, Sunlit Wheat and Starshine Ocean siblings. All four share the Sellita SW200 Elaboré automatic movement (41h power reserve) in the brand's 38mm 316L steel case, sapphire crystal front and back, and 50m water resistance. At research time all four colorways were in stock at $2,592, the brand's current top-selling price tier.

Yellow Track (formerly listed here as "Track Compass") uses a dry-sifted, opaque mustard-yellow enamel dial fired to a uniform matte finish, paired with a vintage track-style railway minute ring for a sense of motion. It runs the brand's Sellita SW200 Elaboré automatic movement (28,800 vph, 41-hour power reserve, ±7 s/d accuracy) in a 38mm 316L steel case with sapphire crystal front and back and 50m water resistance; sibling colorway Galaxy shares the same case and dial layout in a mineral-flecked black enamel.

Desert Brown uses the traditional Grand Feu enamel-over-silver-leaf technique in warm brown tones with authentic Ancient Greek numeral markers, part of the same "Smoked Ocean" enamel styling used across its Glacier Blue and Seagrass Green siblings (Seagrass Green's dial is literally printed "Smoked Ocean"). All three share the brand's 38mm 316L steel case, sapphire crystal front and back, 50m water resistance, and Sellita SW200 automatic movement. Seagrass Green is currently sold out while Desert Brown and Glacier Blue remain in stock, priced from $2,092.

Discontinued (2025). The Havana is Furlan Marri's flagship mecha-quartz chronograph and the design that won the brand the GPHG "Horological Revelation" prize in 2021, only seven months after its Kickstarter launch. Its 38mm 316L steel case pairs a Seiko VK64 mecha-quartz movement — sweeping like a mechanical, accurate like a quartz — with a decagonal screwed caseback, engraved 'Tasti Tondi' pushers, and deep case engravings. The Havana Salmon colorway became the brand's signature piece and a fast riser on the secondary market; newer dial variants such as Castagna, Rosso Grigio, Nero Sabbia, Sabbia Rosa, and Ardesia Blu remain in current production.

The Sector line is Furlan Marri's move into automatic three-hand watchmaking, built around 'cow horns'/Cornes de Vache-style lugs borrowed from classic vintage dress-watch design. Each 37.5mm 316L steel case houses a Swiss-made La Joux-Perret G100 automatic movement with a tungsten rotor, palladium coating, hacking seconds, and a 68-hour power reserve. Every Sector ships with two interchangeable straps, one curved and one straight, fitted through twin lug holes.

Discontinued (2024). The Flyback collection is Furlan Marri's mechanical chronograph statement, developed with Revolution Watch and collector Auro Montanari and limited to 300 pieces per colorway. Its 38mm steel case houses a manually wound, column-wheel flyback chronograph caliber based on the Sellita 5100, delivering a 63-hour power reserve and a pulsometer scale on the dial. Salmon Flyback, Honey Blue Flyback, and Taupe Flyback each sold out shortly after release, making the series one of the brand's most collectible mechanical drops.

Discontinued (2025). Disco Volante is Furlan Marri's manually wound dress watch, its rounded 38mm steel case with hidden lugs and a curved bezel nodding to mid-century 'flying saucer' case design. It runs on a Peseux 7001 hand-wound movement, redesigned and finished entirely by hand in Geneva, delivering a 42-hour power reserve in an ultra-thin build. Gem-set editions such as Disco Onyx Diamonds, and one-off art collaborations like Disco Stromatolite, have since extended the line beyond its original three-color run.

The Smokey Bear Watch is VERO's officially licensed collaboration with the U.S. Forest Service and the Smokey Bear mascot, with 10% of every sale going back to wildfire prevention and forest conservation. The debut Smokey '44 references 1944, the year Smokey Bear's ad campaign began, while later editions reuse the same 38mm field-watch case in different finishes: the '64, bronze-cased 80th Anniversary pieces, the Campfire Edition, and the Blue Skies Edition. Every version runs a Seiko NH38A automatic movement with a 41-hour power reserve behind an AR-coated sapphire crystal, with a screw-down crown and case back rated to 120m.

The Workhorse Chrono is VERO's standalone field chronograph, built around a 44.5mm stainless steel case finished in color-tinted, scratch-resistant Cerakote and wrapped in rubberized steel bullhorn guards. It runs a Miyota 6S21 left-handed quartz chronograph movement with a one-hour timer, behind an AR-coated sapphire crystal, with a triple-gasket screw-down crown and 120m water resistance. The same case was reissued for the VERO x Scout Motors collaboration in Terra Cotta and Moonstone Blue, colors drawn from the Scout II and Scout 80's original paint codes.

The VERO x Realtree Tide Tracker pairs a 39.5mm case with a dual 120-click bezel that tracks high and low tides up to 14 days out. Each colorway comes on a canvas strap printed with an original Realtree camouflage pattern and is powered by a Japanese-made Seiko NH38A automatic movement regulated to +/-10 seconds per day. Cases are 316L stainless steel (matte black DLC-coated steel on the Midnight Edition) with an AR-coated flat sapphire crystal and 120m water resistance.

The One Moto Solar was built as the official timepiece of the 16th annual One Motorcycle Show in Portland, Oregon, where VERO served as timekeeper. Its 38mm stainless steel case has a scratch-resistant DLC coating and houses a Seiko solar-powered movement rated for roughly a four-month power reserve on a full UV charge. It ships on a perforated leather racing strap in dark brown or light tan, with an AR-coated flat sapphire crystal and 100m water resistance.

The Studio Edition is VERO's first collaboration with Portland custom tailor Wildwood & Company, designed to pair with bespoke suits while keeping VERO's usual durability standards. It uses a 38mm case in bronze or stainless steel on a cross-stitched Italian Saffiano leather strap with a deployant clasp, powered by a Seiko NH38A automatic movement with a 41-hour power reserve. The case backs and crowns screw down for 120m water resistance behind an AR-coated flat sapphire crystal, and the run was limited to 200 units online.

watches.crystal: Box sapphire crystal, antiglare with 8-layer AR coating
watches.description: The Photic MKII is Clemence's dive watch, built around a 38.5mm 316L steel case (39mm across the bezel) with a 904L bezel ring, precision ball-bearing click and domed sapphire insert, driven by a high-beat automatic Miyota 9039 regulated to +/-12 seconds a day. It is rated to 200m water resistance, shielded against magnetic fields over 25,000 A/m, and finished with an antiglare box sapphire crystal and Grade A BGW9 lume. The watch has drawn wide praise from watch press including Fratello Watches, Worn & Wound and The Deep Track for its finishing and value.

watches.crystal: Box sapphire crystal, antiglare with 8-layer AR coating
watches.description: The Munro is Clemence's field watch, hand-assembled in Britain with a 37.5mm, 9.25mm-thick 316L steel case and a high-beat automatic Miyota 9039 movement regulated to +/-12 seconds a day. It carries an antiglare box sapphire crystal with 8 internal AR-coating layers, Grade A BGW9 lume-filled hands and markers, and is rated to 150m water resistance. Reviewers have singled out its tapering, tool-less micro-adjust steel bracelet as exceptional value at the price.

watches.crystal: Double dome sapphire, internal anti-reflective coating
watches.description: A 41mm dive watch in a lightweight Grade 5 titanium case rated to 300m, with a unidirectional brushed ceramic bezel and the automatic Miyota 9039 inside.
A 36.5mm three-hander inspired by 1940s design: five-piece stepped case, sector dial with railway-track minute ring, and the automatic Miyota 8315 with a 60-hour reserve.

watches.crystal: Double dome sapphire, internal anti-reflective coating
watches.description: A 36mm cocktail dress watch with a genuine cut natural-stone dial — a different mineral slab per piece — in a 9.2mm steel-and-titanium case, hand-wound by the Swiss La Joux-Perret D100.

A California-dial manual-wind dress watch hand-assembled and regulated in VERO's Portland workshop around a Swiss Sellita SW-210-01, with black-rhodium plating and blued screws under an exhibition caseback.

watches.caseMaterial: Stainless steel with Cerakote ceramic coating
watches.description: Developed with the U.S. Forest Service: a Cerakote-coated field watch on a self-charging Seiko Kinetic movement, assembled in Portland, with case colors keyed to wildland-fire roles and a portion of sales supporting conservation work.

Trafford's first always-in-stock Daytripper — one Blue colorway sold outside the usual limited seasonal drops, going live July 22, 2026 with first shipments in September. Same Miyota 9075-based movement with an independently adjustable hour hand.

Trafford's first always-in-stock Touring GMT — one White colorway outside the limited seasonal drops, going live July 22, 2026 with first shipments in September. Miyota 9075 true-GMT caliber, sapphire front and rear, date at 6.

watches.crystal: Double-domed sapphire, blue tint, AR coating
watches.description: A Seiko NH35 automatic in a brushed CuSn8 bronze dive case — the crown inset is brass melted down from a century-old British firefighter's helmet, and the seconds track echoes UK fire-engine chequered trim.

watches.crystal: Domed sapphire, blue tint; glass bezel insert
watches.description: A Swiss Sellita SW220 day-date under a green glass dial styled on a fire-exit sign — the day wheel shows the running exit-sign man doing a different action each day, and a rotating caseback disc animates him fleeing a blaze.

watches.crystal: Double-dome sapphire, internal AR coating; sapphire bezel insert
watches.description: The Aquascaphe GMT adds a Swiss Soprod C125 automatic GMT movement to Baltic's dive-watch case, with an independently adjustable GMT hand tracking a second time zone against a 24-click bidirectional bezel with a sapphire insert. The 39mm 316L steel case carries a glossy black dial with a date window at 6 o'clock, and 100m water resistance — reduced from the standard Aquascaphe's 200m to accommodate the GMT crown. Grey, green, and orange colorways differentiate the bezel and GMT hand tint against the shared black dial.

Introduced in 2025 after seven years of the original Aquascaphe, the MK2 keeps a 120-click unidirectional sapphire bezel and Miyota 9039 automatic movement but adds a redesigned case with drilled lugs and refreshed lume-filled indices. It's offered in 37mm and 39.5mm sizes across glossy blue and green, or grained grey and warm silver dials, each paired with a color-matched vulcanized rubber strap. Water resistance holds at 200m under a double-dome sapphire crystal.

The Aquascaphe Bronze swaps the standard model's steel case for CuAl8 bronze, which develops a unique patina with wear, while keeping the 39mm dive-watch proportions, 120-click unidirectional bezel, and Miyota 9039 automatic movement. It's rated to 200m water resistance under a double-dome sapphire crystal and ships on a vulcanized rubber strap with a matching bronze buckle. Black, blue gilt, and brown gradient dials are offered.

Baltic's take on the vintage EPSA compressor case, the Aquascaphe Dual-Crown uses a second, unscrewed crown at 4 o'clock to rotate an internal bidirectional bezel underwater without disturbing the water-resistant winding crown at 3. The uncluttered 39mm steel case — offered in polished steel or black PVD — runs a Miyota 9039 automatic movement, holds 200m water resistance, and is capped with a single-dome sapphire crystal. There's no date window, keeping the dial minimal in line with vintage dive-tool codes.

Originally a limited collaboration with A Collected Man, the MR Roulette joined Baltic's permanent MR line in July 2024, pairing a 36mm steel case with the ultra-thin Hangzhou CAL5000A micro-rotor automatic movement for a 9.9mm profile. The dial combines brushed sectors, a railroad-track minute scale, and an off-center guilloché small-seconds counter under a high-domed hesalite crystal. It's water resistant to 30m and offered in blue, salmon, silver, or black.

Launched in February 2024 as a departure from Baltic's vintage dive-watch catalog, the Prismic pairs a 36mm stainless-steel-and-titanium case with the hand-wound ETA/Peseux 7001, a historic ultra-thin ébauche visible through an exhibition caseback with Côtes de Genève and blued screws. The angular case houses a textured guilloché dial with a brushed sector and a grained small-seconds subdial at 6 o'clock, under a double-dome sapphire crystal. It's rated to 30m water resistance and offered in grey blue, salmon, purple, and green, on a steel mesh bracelet or leather strap.

The Scalegraph's 2025 relaunch bumped water resistance to 100m via screw-down pushers, keeping the hand-wound Sellita SW510-M chronograph movement — a Valjoux 7750-based caliber running at 28,800vph with a 63-hour power reserve. The 39.5mm steel case carries a tricompax layout (30-minute counter at 3, 12-hour counter at 6, small seconds at 9) under a double-dome sapphire crystal, with a brushed aluminum tachymeter bezel. It's offered in metallic champagne, glossy blue, and metallic grey, on leather, rubber, or steel bracelet.

First released in 2019 and since updated to the Miyota 8315 automatic movement, the HMS 002 is a compact 38mm dress watch with a stepped case and an art-deco-inspired sector dial. Its high-domed hesalite crystal, leaf-shaped hands, and matte sandblasted dial finish reference founder Étienne Malec's 1940s-clock inspiration. It's time-only, water resistant to 50m, and backed by a 60-hour power reserve.

Baltic's first worldtimer, the Heures du Monde uses a Soprod C125 GMT movement with a transparent 24-hour disc that makes one rotation per day against a printed city ring on the brushed ceramic bezel, giving worldtimer functionality with GMT-level pricing and complexity. The 37mm steel case houses natural stone dials — labradorite, tiger's eye, or sodalite — each individually patterned, with the first series limited and numbered to 200 pieces per variant. Water resistance is 100m under a double-dome sapphire crystal, with 42 hours of power reserve.

Discontinued (2025). Baltic's founding hand-wound chronograph family, spanning the Bicompax 001, 002, and 003 generations released from its 2017 Kickstarter debut onward. Built around a milled 38mm stepped stainless steel case with twin sub-dials (running seconds and a 30-minute counter), it runs on the Seagull ST19/ST1901 column-wheel caliber with a 42-hour power reserve and a high-domed hesalite crystal. Assembled in France; the line was sold through Baltic's April 2025 catalog reset.

Discontinued (2025). A dressy triple-register chronograph in a 39.5mm stainless steel case, driven by the hand-wound Sellita SW510-M with a 63-hour power reserve, twin sub-dials, and an aluminium tachymeter bezel under a double-domed sapphire crystal. Launched in August 2022 as a 300-piece Baltic x Peter Auto limited edition (numbered 1-300, beige dial with orange/yellow racing accents) before joining the regular collection in Panda and Reverse Panda references. Retired from the Tricompax name in Baltic's 2025 catalog reset and folded into the Scalegraph Classic line.

Discontinued (2025). Trafford's debut model and the original Crossroads before the Swiss-made Crossroads S: a 36mm square-cased three-hander with a custom red rotor visible through an exhibition caseback, offered with either the automatic Miyota 9039 (in-house regulated, 48-hour reserve) or a Seiko VH31 mecha-quartz movement. The 316L steel case is 46mm lug-to-lug and rated to 50m under a sapphire crystal. Sold out and superseded by the Crossroads S.

Discontinued (2022). Clemence's debut dive watch and predecessor to the Photic MKII: a 38.5mm (39mm across the bezel) brushed 316L steel case with a 120-click bezel, domed sapphire insert, and a high-beat automatic Miyota 9039 regulated to +/-12 seconds a day. Rated to 200m water resistance with an exhibition caseback, offered on a steel diver's bracelet or an FKM rubber tropic strap. Funded on Kickstarter in September 2021 and sold out in 2022, making way for the refined Photic MKII.

Discontinued. A 38mm dive watch on Vero's own steel bracelet, built around a Sellita SW200-1 automatic with 200m water resistance and a 60-click unidirectional bezel. The case is media-blasted 316L steel, 10.75mm thick, with a sapphire crystal and internal AR coating. Some colorways Cerakote the bezel to match the dial for a monochrome look; others pair a black DLC bezel with a colored dial.

Discontinued. The larger sibling to the Open Water 38, with an 11mm-thick case, screw-down crown, and a 60-click unidirectional dive bezel over a Sellita SW200-1 automatic. Rated to 200m with a flat sapphire crystal and single-side AR coating, on a steel bracelet. Vero released roughly eight Pacific Northwest-themed colorways over the model's run; four representative ones are listed here.

Discontinued. A 55-piece limited edition built on the Open Water 41 dive platform to commemorate Vero's entry in the Mexican 1000 off-road race, with a cream dial, black DLC bezel, and a perforated Horween leather racing strap in place of the usual steel bracelet. Automatic Sellita SW200-1, 200m water resistance, flat sapphire crystal.

watches.caseMaterial: 316L stainless steel with black DLC coating
watches.description: Discontinued. A slim, unisex quartz sports watch on a contouring silicone strap, sized for smaller wrists at 38mm wide and 12mm thick. Swiss Ronda 763 quartz movement, 200m water resistance, domed sapphire crystal, screw-down crown and caseback. Offered in four dial colorways, each on a black DLC-coated steel case.

Discontinued. Vero's Century Series pairs a Sellita SW200 automatic and display caseback with a clean, mid-century-inspired dial and concentric colored chapter rings, on a leather strap. Offered in 36mm and 40mm case sizes across three dial variants: Crew, Summit, and Tempo. Parts are manufactured and dials printed in Vero's Portland, Oregon shop, with each watch assembled and regulated in-house to +/-5 seconds/day.

Discontinued. The GMT flagship of Vero's SW line, upgrading the base sport watch with a Sellita SW330-1 automatic GMT movement, date window, and a 3-part brass dial with ceramic coating. 41mm black DLC-coated stainless steel case, domed sapphire crystal, and a molded silicone strap. Offered in three two-tone dial/hand colorways.

Discontinued (2026). A numbered follow-up to the 2021 8-Bit chronograph, limited to 300 pieces with a refreshed 3D pixel-textured dial mimicking early arcade-cabinet graphics. Shares the 38mm 316L steel cushion case, Seiko VK64 meca-quartz movement, and quick-release teal leather strap of the original, rated to 50m water resistance. Sold out shortly after its March 2026 launch.

watches.caseMaterial: Brushed 316L stainless steel (black PVD on the 'S')
watches.description: Discontinued. Astor + Banks' first chronograph: a Ronda 5050.B Swiss quartz chrono module in a 44mm brushed 316L steel case with a fixed bezel, big-date window at 6 o'clock, and a screw-down crown. Sold in black, a blue-dial 'Bleu', and an all-black PVD 'S' on canvas, each on a Horween leather strap with a signed butterfly deployment buckle. Sapphire crystal is AR-coated on both faces; water resistant to 10 ATM.

Discontinued. A made-to-order dress watch built on the hand-wound ETA 6497-1, finished with Cotes de Geneve and visible through a sapphire exhibition caseback, with a 46-hour power reserve. The 40mm brushed 316L steel case pairs an off-white dial with blued, heat-treated steel hands, applied Roman numerals, and a small-seconds subdial, on a genuine alligator strap. Water resistant to 50m.

Discontinued. A vintage-inspired pilot's watch: a Swiss automatic movement in a German-made 42mm brushed 316L steel case with a screw-down, diamond-shaped crown and 22mm lugs. The clean three-hand-and-date dial came in black or navy-blue sunray finishes with BGW9/C3 Superluminova markers, on a handmade Horween leather strap; the Pilomatic and Pilomatic B navy were limited runs of 50 pieces, followed by the Pilomatic B2. Water resistant to 20 ATM.

watches.caseMaterial: Brushed 316L stainless steel (German-made case; PVD finish also offered)
watches.description: Discontinued. An early Astor + Banks manual-wind model on a nickel-plated Swiss movement with a 46-hour power reserve and Cotes de Geneve finishing, visible through the exhibition caseback. The 42mm brushed steel case, made in Germany, has an onion-shaped crown and a sandwich dial with a small-seconds subdial at 9 o'clock, offered in black or blue dials with brushed or PVD case finishes. Water resistant to 50m, on a genuine leather strap with a 5-year warranty.

watches.caseMaterial: Brushed 316L stainless steel with polished chamfers ('S' in black DLC)
watches.description: Discontinued. The original Sea Ranger, Astor + Banks' first dive watch and first watch on a bracelet, funded on Kickstarter in 2019. The 40mm brushed 316L steel case (45.5mm lug-to-lug) runs a Sellita SW200 automatic behind a double-domed sapphire crystal, water resistant to 30 ATM, with a 12-hour fully-lumed sapphire bezel and inner 24-hour track that work together as a makeshift second time zone. Came standard on a steel bracelet with rubber and NATO straps included; variants spanned black, blue, the black-DLC 'S', and the white 'Polar Edition'.

Galaxy uses Hora Pictor's vintage track/compass dial layout in black enamel mixed with crushed minerals, ground to a fine, sandy consistency and fired at 800°C for a subtle, shifting cosmic shimmer across the face. It shares the brand's 38mm 316L steel case, Sellita SW200 Elaboré automatic movement (28,800 vph, 41-hour power reserve, ±7 s/d accuracy), sapphire crystal front and back, and 50m water resistance with sibling model Yellow Track. An enamel rotor with a hand-applied breeze texture is integrated into the movement, visible through the sapphire caseback.

Glacier Blue recreates the fracture of a glacier in cool blue Grand Feu enamel interwoven with silver leaf, a texture that shifts from pure glacier blue in cool light to a mysterious green-blue under warm light. It runs a Swiss-made Sellita SW200 automatic movement in a polished 38mm 316L steel case with sapphire crystal front and back and 5ATM (50m) water resistance, paired with white steel hands and a heat-blued seconds hand on a 20mm handmade strap. Hora Pictor backs it with a 3-year warranty.

Starshine Ocean-Origin lays blue enamel over a silver-leaf base, fired at high temperature so the surface sparkles like starlight reflected on the ocean floor. It shares the brand's 38mm 316L steel case, Sellita SW200 Elaboré automatic movement (28,800 vph, 41-hour power reserve, ±7 s/d accuracy), sapphire crystal front and back, and 50m water resistance with siblings Sunlit Wheat-Origin and Twilight Violet-Origin. An enamel rotor with a hand-applied breeze texture is integrated into the movement, visible through the sapphire caseback.

Sunlit Wheat-Origin is inspired by golden wheat fields, its dial hand-enamelled over a silver-leaf base and fired multiple times at high temperature for a brilliant, shimmering golden texture. It shares the brand's 38mm 316L steel case, Sellita SW200 Elaboré automatic movement (28,800 vph, 41-hour power reserve, ±7 s/d accuracy), sapphire crystal front and back, and 50m water resistance with siblings Starshine Ocean-Origin and Twilight Violet-Origin.

Twilight Violet-Origin pairs purple enamel with a silver-leaf base for a deep, luminous lustre that shifts across the dial like dusk settling over a silver horizon. It shares the brand's 38mm 316L steel case, Sellita SW200 Elaboré automatic movement (28,800 vph, 41-hour power reserve, ±7 s/d accuracy), sapphire crystal front and back, and 50m water resistance with siblings Starshine Ocean-Origin and Sunlit Wheat-Origin.

A bronze commemorative watch honoring the Massey Shaw, the historic London fireboat that helped rescue more than 600 Allied troops during the 1940 Dunkirk evacuation. The 42mm CuSn8 bronze case houses a Sellita SW200 Top Grade automatic movement (26 jewels, 38-hour power reserve) rated to 50m water resistance under a blue-tinted sapphire crystal. Its dial reproduces the ship's engine-room telegraph, with "STOP" and "LONDON" picked out in red, and the caseback encloses a genuine fragment of the Massey Shaw's original engine beneath an engraved evacuation scene. Limited to 600 pieces — one for every soldier the vessel is credited with saving.

A paired dive-watch duo built on William Wood's Valiant-derived 41mm steel case: the Fire Watch wears a raging, high-relief flame dial, while the Extinguisher Watch answers with a foam-textured pearlescent white dial. Both run a Seiko NH35 automatic (41-hour power reserve) under a double-domed, blue-tinted sapphire crystal, rated to 100m water resistance with a unidirectional dive bezel. Each crown is cast from brass melted down from a genuine 100-year-old British firefighter's helmet, and straps are cut from upcycled fire hose.

Commemorates the 25th anniversary of September 11, its dial moulding a New York skyline at night with the Tribute in Light's twin beams rendered in Super-LumiNova that glows blue after dark. The 41mm 316L steel case is finished in black plating with a matching unidirectional bezel, and the 9 and 11 o'clock indices are picked out in rose gold to mark the date. Powered by a Seiko NH35 automatic (41-hour power reserve) under a double-domed sapphire crystal, it is rated to 100m water resistance, and 10% of each sale is donated to the Tunnel to Towers Foundation.

Discontinued. A 41mm 316L steel dive watch inspired by the Great Fire of London of 1666, its dial patterned on the clock face of Big Ben with gothic Roman numerals over a mirrored silver sunburst. A genuine British £2 Great Fire of London commemorative coin is sealed into the caseback under glass. Powered by a Seiko NH35 automatic (41-hour power reserve) rated to 100m water resistance, it was limited to 50 pieces.

Mechaquartz is Furlan Marri's current bread-and-butter chronograph line, built around the Seiko VK64 meca-quartz caliber — a mechanical chronograph module riding on a quartz base, so the pushers and sub-dials feel hand-wound while timekeeping stays quartz-accurate. Each 38mm 316L steel case carries a decagonal screwed caseback, engraved 'Tasti Tondi' round pushers, and a double-domed sapphire crystal with anti-reflective coating, inherited from the brand's original GPHG-recognized chronograph platform. The line runs five colorways — Sabbia Rosa (rose-gold PVD case, champagne dial), Ardesia Blu, Nero Sabbia, Rosso Grigio, and Castagna — each shipping with two quick-release leather straps.

brands.blurb: Named for the Gold Coast street corner where founder Andrew Perez — an Army veteran and lifelong watch nerd — got his start, Astor + Banks assembles every watch in Chicago. Hardened steel, serious anti-magnetic ratings, and clean officer's-watch design at honest prices.

Studio Underd0g was founded in London in 2020 by industrial designer Richard Benc, who sketched the brand's first watch during the March 2020 lockdown and posted it to a watch-enthusiast Facebook group to an unexpectedly huge response. The name plays on "underdog" — a design-led challenger among the big Swiss houses — with a gamer-style "0" swapped in for the "o". Every watch is hand-assembled start-to-finish by a single technician in Great Britain, and the brand has built its following on pun-named dial colorways (Watermel0n, Pink Lem0nade) and headline collaborations with Moser, Fears, and Massena LAB.

Founded in Paris in 2016 by Etienne Malec, who grew up immersed in his late father's diary cataloguing a lifelong watch collection, Baltic takes its name from his father's roots on Poland's Baltic coast. The brand went public via a Kickstarter campaign in April 2017, pre-selling 1,200 watches of its debut Bicompax and HMS models and raising nearly 8x its goal. Baltic designs vintage-inspired watches assembled and adjusted at its own atelier in Besançon, France, and sells direct-to-consumer to avoid traditional retail markups.

Trafford Watch Co. was founded in 2020 by Nathan Trafford, a designer originally from northern England now based in Austin, Texas, who started the brand to create 'something tangible that lasts.' Its Austin-designed, overseas-manufactured watches lean on narrative color palettes drawn from Texas Hill Country wildflowers (Crossroads), classic rock guitars (Touring GMT), and WWII racing-driver spies (S.O.E. Roadster), earning coverage from Worn & Wound, Watch Clicker, and Teddy Baldassarre.

Founded in 2017 by Jonny Garrett and named for his grandfather William Wood, a Newcastle & Gateshead firefighter who passed away in 2009, the British independent watchmaker builds every piece from genuine upcycled firefighting materials. Straps are cut from retired fire hose, and several collections cast a coin or crown from brass melted down from a century-old firefighter's helmet.

Brew Watch Co. was founded in 2015 by industrial designer Jonathan Ferrer, who launched the brand from New York City via Kickstarter after noticing how baristas timed espresso extraction. Every design decision traces back to that coffee ritual: chronograph totalizers sized to a 25-35 second espresso pour, cushion cases inspired by vintage espresso machines and Art Deco cafes, and a coffee-bean logomark on the crown and dial.

O&HoraPictor (Latin: 'painter of time') was founded in Hong Kong in 2024 by enamel artist Eriks, growing out of his enamel atelier Studio Orodol, established in 2017. Every dial is individually hand-fired Grand Feu or cloisonné enamel over silver leaf, paired with a Swiss Sellita SW200 automatic movement in a 38mm steel case.

Founded in Geneva in 2021 by Swiss designer Andrea Furlan and Saudi Arabian collector Hamad Al Marri, Furlan Marri won the GPHG "Horological Revelation" prize just seven months after its Kickstarter launch for its neo-vintage mecha-quartz chronographs. The brand has since expanded from mecha-quartz into automatic and hand-wound mechanical watches while keeping its 1940s-1950s-inspired design language.

VERO Watch Company was founded in Portland, Oregon in 2015 by watch enthusiasts Chris Boudreaux and Danny Recordon, who wanted well-made watches without a luxury price tag. The brand still assembles, services, and warranties every watch out of its Portland shop, and its current catalog leans heavily on licensed and brand collaborations, including Smokey Bear/US Forest Service, Realtree, and Scout Motors.

brands.knownFor: climate-positive British field and dive watches
brands.blurb: Founded in Edinburgh in 2021 by ecologist Tom Clemence, whose late grandfather's Universal Genève watch sparked his love of horology, Clemence designs and hand-assembles its watches in Britain. The brand plants a native Scottish tree for every watch sold and offsets at least twice each watch's carbon footprint, funded by accepting smaller margins rather than raising prices.
